A pseudo-staminode is a structure that looks like a staminode but is not a sterile stamen. Mapping it to staminode (PO_0009077) loses the 'not a stamen' meaning. It is better left unmapped.
Same as R2353: a pseudo-staminodium is not a true staminode.
A syncarp is a fruit formed from fused carpels, or a multiple fruit. Fruit is the right part.
In French, 'syncarpe' is often the adjective for a gynoecium or ovary with fused carpels ('ovaire syncarpe'), not the fruit. Match it only when it is a noun for the fruit.
The plural of syncarp, a fruit. An English adjective plural is unlikely.
PO gives 'vein' as a synonym of vascular bundle. The 'major' rank is lost but the part is right.
Corona segments are the parts of a corona (as in Asclepiadaceae and Passiflora), which fits corona lobe.
The plural of corona segment.
'vitae' is a variant spelling of 'vittae', the plural of vitta (oil tube in Apiaceae fruits).
Receptacular scales (paleae or chaff in Asteraceae) are a synonym of flower bract (chaff) in PO.
The plural of receptacular scale.
The French form of receptacular scale (palea).
A receptacle tube is the hypanthium, the floral cup (as in Myrtaceae and Rosaceae).
Same as R2365, with a space instead of a hyphen.
A strand is a portion of sclerenchyma tissue. PO lists 'portion of sclerenchyma tissue' as a synonym.
The plural of sclerenchyma strand.
Another phrasing of sclerenchyma strand.
The replum is the persistent partition of a fruit (as in Brassicaceae).
'repla' is the plural of replum.
PO's 'sporangium neck' synonym fits the apophysis of a moss capsule. In angiosperm fruits a 'capsule neck' is not a sporangium base.
Same as R2372.

PO gives 'cone scale' as a synonym of megasporophyll (ovuliferous scale). Scales of pollen cones are microsporophylls, so the rule is correct only for seed cones.
Same as R2375.
The leaf axis of a compound leaf or frond is the rachis.
The plural of leaf axis.
The French plural of leaf axis.

'Stamen tube' means the same as staminal tube.
The plural of stamen tube.
The French form of staminal tube.
The French form of staminal tube, with the feminine ending.
'arista' is a synonym of awn in PO. The plural 'aristae' is also an awn.
'aristés' is the French adjective 'awned', not the noun. It describes a feature (awn present) and is not a part to use as a bearer. It should be an entity-presence rule for awn.
Underleaves are the ventral leaves of liverworts, a kind of non-vascular leaf. The ventral position is lost, but no more specific class exists.
The plural of underleaf.
An offset is a short lateral shoot from the base of the plant. This is close to a basal axillary shoot (PO synonyms: tiller and ratoon).
The plural of offset.
Involucral leaves are the bracts of the involucre.
The plural of involucral leaf.
These are the involucral bracts of the primary umbel or head. The 'primary' rank is lost but the part is right.
'viscidia' is the Latin plural of viscidium.

A segment of a leaf blade is a division of the lamina, which fits leaf lamina lobe. In palms and compound leaves it may mean a leaflet.
